S002.name: Sustained_Attention_Difficulty
S002.description: Often has difficulty sustaining attention in tasks or play activities.
examples: Focuses at first during class or meetings but soon becomes distracted or spaces out.
Re-reads the same paragraph in a book multiple times but the content does not register.
Loses focus while watching movies or TV and misses the plot.
Unable to maintain attention until the end of a long meeting or lecture, often drifting off or becoming drowsy.

S004.name: Instruction_Follow through_Difficulty
S004.description: Often does not follow through on instructions and fails to finish schoolwork, chores, or duties in the workplace.
examples: Starts homework or projects but fails to complete them, submitting unfinished work or missing deadlines.
When given multi-step instructions, follows only the first few steps and forgets the rest.
Starts cleaning or organizing but switches to another task midway, failing to finish.
Leaves almost completed work reports or paperwork unfinished, neglecting the final steps.

S005.name: Organization_Difficulty
S005.description: Often has difficulty organizing tasks and activities.
examples: Desk, bag, or room is always messy and remains disorganized.
Unable to prioritize or determine the order of tasks, starting them randomly.
Fails to plan time effectively, frequently missing deadlines or rushing to finish at the last minute.
Feels overwhelmed by how to start multi-step projects and procrastinates.

S010.name: Fidgeting
S010.description: Often fidgets with or taps hands or feet or squirms in seat.
examples: Constantly shaking legs or twisting and squirming body while seated.
Spinning a pen or fiddling with nearby objects, unable to keep hands still.
Continually changing posture and feeling uncomfortable while sitting.
Constantly moving, such as tapping the desk with fingers or tapping feet on the floor.

S011.name: Leaving_Seat
S011.description: Often leaves seat in situations when remaining seated is expected.
examples: Frequently leaves seat or wanders around during class or meetings using excuses.
Unable to sit still during meals and keeps getting up.
Leaves seat in the middle of a movie or performance to go to the restroom or go outside.
Continually leaves seat and wanders around in the office where one is expected to sit and work.

S012.name: Feeling_Restless
S012.description: Often runs about or climbs in situations where it is inappropriate. (Note: In adolescents or adults, may be limited to feeling restless.)
examples: Feels uncomfortable and restless as if something is squirming inside when sitting still.
Feels internally anxious and stifled in situations requiring prolonged sitting.
A sense of urgency and anxiety that one must keep moving or doing something.
Feels unable to endure staying still and must constantly be doing something.

S016.name: Blurting_Answers
S016.description: Often blurts out an answer before a question has been completed.
examples: Raises hand or blurts out the answer before the question is even finished in class or meetings.
Jumps to conclusions and speaks before the other person finishes their sentence.
Answers hastily without reading the question to the end in quizzes or exams.
Interrupts and answers in the middle of a conversation without listening to the other person until the end.

S017.name: Waiting_Turn_Difficulty
S017.description: Often has difficulty waiting his or her turn.
examples: Cannot wait and cuts in line or gets impatient when standing in a queue.
Rushes or cuts in without waiting for their turn in games or board games.
Keeps checking the time or complaining when waiting for their turn at hospitals or public offices.
Fidgets, complains, or gets annoyed in situations where waiting for a turn is required.

symptom.disease_info: Attention-Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder (Predominantly Hyperactive/Impulsive Presentation) is characterized mainly by developmentally inappropriate levels of motor activity, restlessness, impulsive decision-making, and difficulty inhibiting responses, with inattention often present but less prominent. It typically begins in childhood and persists into adolescence and adulthood, with functional impairment in academic, occupational, or social domains required for diagnosis. Clinically, patients may come to attention when environmental demands for sustained effort, planning, or behavioral restraint increase, such as during higher education or more complex jobs. It is distinguished from mood, anxiety, or disruptive behavior disorders by its early onset, cross-situational pervasiveness, and the pattern of chronic hyperactive/impulsive traits rather than episodic changes in behavior.

patient.stressor: For most of his life, Edgar’s constant motion and spur-of-the-moment decisions were absorbed by informal jobs, family events, and church activities where structure was loose and others quietly redirected him. Over the past two years, escalating financial pressure on his household pushed him to take on more responsibility managing his family’s tight budget, coordinating his church’s food pantry logistics, and trying to secure a steady position as a community-center aide. The increased need to sit through planning meetings, handle detailed forms, and wait in lines for assistance programs clashed with his tendency to act before thinking, leading to missed benefits, errors in paperwork, and impulsive small purchases that undermined his carefully tracked spreadsheets, all of which heightened his anxiety about providing for his family. After a near eviction scare triggered by a series of impulsive financial decisions and missed appointments, his wife and parish priest both urged him to seek professional help, and he agreed when he realized his difficulty holding back and staying on track was directly jeopardizing their already fragile finances.
patient.chief_complaint: “When there’s a line or a process, I just can’t seem to wait my turn without jumping ahead or changing plans, and it keeps messing up our money and appointments.”

S002.name: Sustained_Attention_Difficulty
S002.description: Often has difficulty sustaining attention in tasks or play activities.
S002.manifestation: When I sit down to go over the bills or those forms for the assistance office, I’m paying attention for a few minutes and then my mind just drifts off to the birds outside or some song in my head, and when I look back I realize I don’t even remember what line I was on and have to start over again and again.

S004.name: Instruction_Follow through_Difficulty
S004.description: Often does not follow through on instructions and fails to finish schoolwork, chores, or duties in the workplace.
S004.manifestation: My wife will ask me to call about the rent help, then stop by the church pantry to check the schedule, and by the time I’ve started the first thing I’ve already gotten sidetracked talking to someone or checking something else, and I end up coming home with only half of it done or not done at all, even though I honestly meant to finish everything.

S005.name: Organization_Difficulty
S005.description: Often has difficulty organizing tasks and activities.
S005.manifestation: When I try to plan out the week—what day to go to the office, what day to help at church, what day to look for work—I just stare at the paper feeling lost, jumping from one idea to another, and I usually end up doing things last minute or forgetting something important like a deadline for turning in a form.

S010.name: Fidgeting
S010.description: Often fidgets with or taps hands or feet or squirms in seat.
S010.manifestation: Anytime I’m in a meeting at the community center or even just sitting in church, my legs are bouncing, my fingers are tapping on the table or my Bible, and I keep shifting in my seat so much that people next to me sometimes give me that look like, ‘Can you sit still?’ but I just can’t relax my body.

S011.name: Leaving_Seat
S011.description: Often leaves seat in situations when remaining seated is expected.
S011.manifestation: During those long waits at the benefits office, I keep popping up from my chair to pace around, look at the posters, or go outside for a minute even though I know they could call my number while I’m gone, but sitting still in that chair the whole time feels almost impossible.

S012.name: Feeling_Restless
S012.description: Often runs about or climbs in situations where it is inappropriate. (Note: In adolescents or adults, may be limited to feeling restless.)
S012.manifestation: Most days, especially when I’m supposed to be sitting at the kitchen table doing paperwork or helping my son with homework, I feel this buzzing inside like I’ve got to get up and move or do something else right now, and it makes me feel trapped and jumpy if I try to just sit there.

S016.name: Blurting_Answers
S016.description: Often blurts out an answer before a question has been completed.
S016.manifestation: In meetings about the food pantry or talking with the lady at the housing office, I find myself jumping in with answers or finishing their sentences before they’re done explaining, and then I realize I didn’t actually listen to the whole question and I’ve given the wrong information or agreed to something I didn’t fully understand.

S017.name: Waiting_Turn_Difficulty
S017.description: Often has difficulty waiting his or her turn.
S017.manifestation: When I’m standing in line to talk to someone about our rent or to sign up for help, I get so impatient and antsy that I start trying to squeeze ahead, go to a different window, or leave and come back later, and that jumping around has made me lose my spot or even miss my turn more than once, which has really hurt us with the money stuff.

add_requirements.onset_prior_to_12_years: Even back in elementary school, teachers were always calling my mom because I wouldn’t stay in my seat, blurted things out in class, and kept getting sent into the hallway for talking and moving around too much.
add_requirements.functional_impairment: Because I can’t sit still, wait my turn, or follow through on plans, I’ve missed appointments, lost out on benefits we qualified for, and blown parts of our tight budget, which has put my family at real risk of falling behind on rent and bills.
add_requirements.duration: These problems with getting restless, acting before I think, and not being able to stick with tasks have been really causing trouble with our finances and appointments for a little over two years now, ever since I started taking on more of the money and paperwork responsibilities at home.
